effectiveness: Telex records themes — 'Tisza-adó', war and pension fear, and mockery of Magyar Péter in over half the corpus — but makes no persuasion claim; the campaign these videos served lost.
summary: The hard measurement of the domestic AI layer: a named newsroom systematically coded ~200 videos pushing Fidesz and government narratives on Facebook over four months and found 84.3% were created entirely with AI, for 113 million combined impressions. Only 11 of the 200 were paid ads — after Meta's October 2025 EU political-ads ban the material travelled organically instead. This is the entry the site's domestic-share figures are generated from.
caveats: A coded sample of one newsroom's collection, not a census of all pro-government video.
'Entirely AI-generated' is a production judgement by the coders, not a detection-tool output.
Reach is impressions, which is not persuasion — see effectiveness-evidence.

coordination_claimed: explicitly ruled out by the source — Euronews: 'There is no evidence, however, that Fidesz is behind this social media campaign.'

effectiveness: The claim was contradicted by Tisza's own manifesto. Fidesz campaigned on the same premise and lost.
summary: The clearest documented case of convergence without contact. A fabricated claim that Péter Magyar planned to reintroduce conscription was pushed by Storm-1516 through six purpose-built websites and Facebook ads — and, separately, manufactured domestically: in October 2025 Fidesz's youth wing clipped a Ruszin-Szendi video to strip the opening qualifier from 'today, the situation in Hungary is not such that, in optimal circumstances, we should reintroduce mandatory military service', after which the truncated quote appeared in an official government pamphlet and inside a NEM AI video. Two production lines, one frame, no demonstrated link — the source states plainly there is no evidence Fidesz is behind the Russian campaign.
caveats: This is narrative overlap, not a link. The source explicitly rules out evidence of Fidesz being behind the Storm-1516 campaign.
The domestic version has its own fully documented manufacturing history, which is what makes independent origin the most parsimonious reading.
Displayed on the convergence bench but never counted in either technique bucket.

summary: The hardest documented input-side link between Russian officialdom and Hungarian pro-government media — and a demonstration of how narrow such links actually are. Emails obtained by Direkt36 show the Russian military attaché sent a Fidesz-media security commentator two briefing documents, arranged his attendance at the Russian MoD's Moscow security conference (where he pledged by email to 'publish the results on TV and newspapers in Hungary'), and invited him to a farewell reception. Direkt36 reports a high level of textual and thematic overlap in his subsequent analyses — not verbatim copying, and no command-and-control.
caveats: This is one commentator, not an institutional channel. No claim is made that the outlets carrying him knew.
'Closely mirrored' and 'high textual and thematic overlap' are the source's words; they are not evidence of dictation.
